entities.name: Diary of Anne Frank
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Diary of Anne Frank was a personal and poignant record of life in hiding during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Created by Anne Frank in 1942, it details her daily experiences as a 13-year-old Jewish girl living with her family in secret to evade persecution. The diary chronicles their struggles, fears, and hopes for survival, offering a unique insight into the human cost of the Holocaust. Its significance extends beyond its personal context, influencing generations of readers and scholars alike. It has been translated into over 60 languages and remains one of the most widely read and studied diaries in history.

The diary's significance lies in its ability to convey the emotional and psychological toll of living under occupation, as well as its impact on the world stage. The Frank family's experiences are a testament to the resilience of human spirit in the face of unimaginable adversity. The diary has been the subject of numerous adaptations, interpretations, and scholarly analyses, cementing its place in the annals of modern history.

The diary's legacy extends beyond its literary significance, serving as a powerful educational tool for understanding the Holocaust and its consequences. It has also inspired countless works of art, literature, and music, ensuring its relevance to contemporary audiences.

One striking statistic is that over 10 million copies of the diary have been sold worldwide, making it one of the best-selling books of all time. A direct attributed quote from Anne Frank reads: 'In spite of everything, I still believe that people are truly good at heart.'

This enduring cultural footprint is a testament to the power of Anne Frank's story to transcend time and geography, speaking directly to hearts around the world.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "The Diary of a Young Girl (Dutch: Het Achterhuis, 'The Secret Annex'), commonly known as The Diary of Anne Frank, is the personal diary of Annelies Marie Frank (1929–1945), a German-born Jewish girl who hid with her family in a concealed set of rooms (the Secret Annex, 'Achterhuis') in a warehouse at Prinsengracht 263 in Amsterdam from 6 July 1942 to 4 August 1944 — when they were discovered by the Gestapo and deported to Nazi concentration camps. Anne Frank wrote the diary between 12 June 1942 and 1 August 1944 in Dutch, initially in a red-and-white plaid autograph book, later in loose sheets; it was recovered from the Secret Annex after the arrest by Miep Gies (one of the helpers) and preserved. Anne died of typhus at Bergen-Belsen concentration camp in February or March 1945, weeks before the camp's liberation. Her father Otto Frank — the only member of the family to survive — had the diary published in 1947 as Het Achterhuis, translated into English in 1952, and subsequently into over 70 languages.

The Diary is one of the most widely read books in the world — over 35 million copies sold, translated into more than 70 languages — and the most widely read first-hand account of the Holocaust. Anne writes with remarkable intelligence, emotional depth, and literary self-awareness about life in hiding (the claustrophobia, the tensions, the fear, the daily routines), her developing inner life and intellectual ambitions, her first experience of love (with Peter van Pels), and her determined belief in human goodness despite the evidence around her — her famous last lines before arrest: 'I keep my ideals, because in spite of everything I still believe that people are really good at heart.' The combination of its intimate, personal voice, its historical testimony, and Anne's tragic fate have made the Diary one of the most powerful documents of the 20th century.

The Diary of Anne Frank has had enormous cultural impact — the Broadway play (1955, Pulitzer Prize) and film (1959) gave it a global audience; it has been a foundational text of Holocaust education in schools worldwide; and Anne Frank's face has become the most widely recognised symbol of the Holocaust's child victims — a humanising counterweight to the impersonal scale of six million deaths.", "subjects": ["Holocaust", "Modern Era", "World War II", "Netherlands", "Autobiography", "Jewish History", "20th Century", "Holocaust Education"], "frameworks": ["CAUSE_AND_EFFECT", "STRUCTURAL_ANALYSIS"], "historicalSignificance": {"significanceScore": 7, "significanceNarrative": "The Diary of Anne Frank is a testament to the resilience of human spirit in the face of unimaginable adversity, offering a powerful and poignant record of life under occupation.", "significanceCategory": "regional"}, "_editLog": [{"timestamp": "2026-05-17T07:53:25Z", "editorId": "ollama/llama3.2:3b·local·manasa151-MS-7C56", "field": "summary", "oldValue": "Famous diary of a 13-year old dutch jewish girl hiding from the nazis to escape the holocaust Created by Anne Frank.
